summary: amcache_dest_dir_is_safe() verified the scratch directory's owner/DACL/reparse status by PATH (GetNamedSecurityInfoW/GetFileAttributesW), then the subsequent CopyFileW re-resolved the destination by a SEPARATE path -- a TOCTOU window where the verified directory could be deleted/replaced between the two path resolutions, letting an attacker with delete-child rights on the parent directory swap in their own object after the check passed.
trigger: an actor with FILE_DELETE_CHILD on the scratch directory's parent deletes and recreates the directory (or a junction) between amcache_dest_dir_is_safe() returning true and the subsequent CopyFileW
disposition_note: fixed in 85ae9dbd3: open_amcache_dest_dir_handle() opens the directory once via CreateFileW without FILE_SHARE_DELETE and amcache_dest_dir_is_safe() now verifies via GetSecurityInfo/GetFileInformationByHandle against that HANDLE; collect_amcache holds the handle open through the entire copy sequence. Windows refuses delete/rename of the object while the handle is open, so the verified object is provably the same one copied into. Re-reviewed by the same reporter after the fix: confirmed closed for the delete+recreate and in-place-reparse-conversion attack shapes; one narrower residual (FileDispositionInfoEx POSIX-delete semantics, a non-default API) remains and does not block.

summary: The ACE-walk loop only inspects ACCESS_ALLOWED_ACE_TYPE; ACCESS_ALLOWED_OBJECT_ACE_TYPE/ACCESS_ALLOWED_CALLBACK_ACE_TYPE (also grant-bearing) are silently skipped via `continue`.
trigger: a DACL containing an object/callback-type ALLOW ACE granting access to an untrusted principal
adjudicated_by: claude (self, non-CRITICAL/HIGH finding, no separation required per Gate 7)
adjudication_rationale: Reporter's own analysis caps this at I9/E6: the preceding owner check already requires SYSTEM/Administrators ownership, and an unprivileged creator cannot forge that owner field or add an object/callback ACE without WRITE_DAC (which only the owner holds by default) -- so the gap is unreachable given the owner gate already in place. Correctly handling object-ACE variants requires parsing a different, longer struct layout (extra GUID fields before the SID); doing that hastily under time pressure risked introducing a new bug for a scenario the reporter itself assessed as not independently exploitable. Deferred rather than fixed.
